business_scope.primary_industry_name: Mail-Order Retail with Cash on Delivery Settlement

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union (provisional application 2017)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) (2018)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA) (2014)
Canada-China Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income (1986)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA); Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-317; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46; Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44 (CBCA) as amended by Budget Implementation Act, 2023, No. 1, SC 2023, c 26; beneficial ownership transparency requirements under CBCA section 21.1 and associated regulations; applicable Alberta Corporate Registry policies on shareholder records. The UBO threshold is 25% ownership or control, aligned with FATF Recommended Interpretive Note.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original certificate of incorporation or comparable registration of the foreign parent or founding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies or equivalent corporate registry in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if originating state is party; otherwise consular legalization at the Canadian embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance for foreign corporate shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) identification and ownership structure declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or CPA/certified corporate services provider in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and address proof for all proposed directors, shareholders and beneficiaries
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or national identity issuing authority in the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copies with Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter verifying foreign bank relationships and source of funding for investment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Compliance officer of the financial institution holding the funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank letter with apostille or consular legalization if bank charter requires; otherwise direct compliance verification

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of directors, shareholders, UBOs, authorized signatories and counterparties against the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) sanctions list, Public Safety Canada's consolidated sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HMT sanctions list, and Alberta legislative sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act (SC 1992, c 17) and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (SC 2017, c 20). Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates must undergo enhanced due diligence as defined by FINTRAC and FATF Recommendation 12, including source of wealth and source of funds verification. All screening must be repeated after identifying any material change in ownership or control.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry system (CORES) and NUANS Name Search
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English or French alphabetic characters; names may include numerals and limited punctuation. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated or translated into English or French before filing. The name must not be identical to or be confusingly similar with an existing corporate name, trade-mark, or name reserved by another entity. Designations 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.' or equivalent must be included and must not be misleading regarding the entity's structure.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal, the applicant or its corporate agent must file a written request for reconsideration with the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days, attaching a fresh NUANS report and legal submissions demonstrating distinguishability. If the refusal is sustained, the applicant may apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review. Name reservations may be renewed before expiry if no rejection has been issued.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is generally acceptable for maintaining a registered office in Alberta if it is a real street address located in Alberta and service of process can be served at that address; a post office box alone is prohibited. For mail-order retail and cash-on-delivery e-commerce, banking AML/KYC and payment processor due diligence from Airwallex or logistics remittance providers will usually require more than a virtual office, including evidence of operating premises, documentary retention capability, and a physical or verifiable business location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-high for cash-on-delivery e-commerce: estimated 10-20% annual probability of an unannounced inspection by Alberta Corporate Registry, municipal licensing authorities, or CRA during the first year of operation, increasing to 25-35% if GST/HST audits, cash transaction volumes, or cross-border remittance indicators trigger enhanced review.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Alberta Corporate Regulation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NUANS corporate name search and name reservation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff plus registered service charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial fee schedule plus statutory apostille / consular tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External Canadian legal opinion on stage-1 incorporation, ISIC 4791 e-commerce scope and Alberta regulatory compliance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Canadian law firm / barrister and solicitor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark / professional hourly rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate registry filing agent fee for coordinating Alberta incorporation and post-filing initial annual return
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized corporate registry agent in Alberta

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), ss. 6-12 (Articles of Incorporation), s. 9 (Certificate of Incorporation), s. 104 (resident Canadian directors), s. 204 (registered office); Business Corporations Regulation, AR 172/2001.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (Government of Alberta); online filing via Corporate Access / ARIEL portal or paper submission at the Registry counter.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Alberta Corporate Registry prescribed form; electronic filing through Corporate Access or paper filing).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under ABCA; authorized capital is established in the Articles (e.g., unlimited common shares) with consideration fixed by directors. No escrow account is statutorily required for share subscriptions; COD settlement funds held by payment processors are governed by commercial escrow and AML arrangements, not statutory capital escrow.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED: (1) Share Subscription — that the subscriptions recorded in the share subscription ledger be accepted and that share certificates be issued to the subscribers named therein upon receipt of full consideration; (2) Registered Office — that the registered office of the Corporation be established at the address recorded with the Alberta Corporate Registry and that the named registered agent be appointed; (3) Officers — that the following persons be appointed officers of the Corporation: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each to hold office until successors are appointed; (4) Banking — that the President and Treasurer be authorized to open bank accounts, engage payment processors for cash-on-delivery settlement, and execute all instruments to carry out the foregoing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Pre-Incorporation Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (NUANS name search administered through authorized service providers under the ABCA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report for the proposed corporate name. Verify distinctiveness and compliance with ABCA ss. 10-11 and the Business Names Regulation. Secure a name reservation if required, or proceed with a proposed name accepted by the Registry. Confirm that no special consent is required for connotative words.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search request and fee receipt
Proposed corporate name details and corporate ID request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusing similarity, obtain a written consent letter from the prior name holder or submit a revised name with a fresh NUANS report; alternatively, request a registry name review decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Corporate Access online portal / Service Alberta counter).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the Articles of Incorporation signed by the incorporator. Specify the authorized share structure (e.g., unlimited common shares). Appoint the first directors (minimum one; if fewer than four directors, at least one must be a resident Canadian). State the initial registered office address. Pay the statutory filing fee and receive the reviewed Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (signed by incorporator, including registered office and first directors)
NUANS name search report or name reservation approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Articles are queried for incomplete director residency declarations or defective share clauses, cure by resubmitting corrected Articles via Corporate Access; the incorporator may withdraw and re-file before certificate issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Records Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / corporate secretary of the Corporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, establish the statutory minute book, adopt By-law No. 1, prepare the registers of directors and shareholders, and order the corporate seal if adopted. Obtain a Certificate of Status for banking and counterparty reliance.
required_dossiers: Minute book with directors' and shareholders' registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry records contain typographical errors, file a Statement of Correction with the Registrar; request a certified Certificate of Status for third-party reliance in the interim.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or adopt a unanimous written resolution under ABCA s. 121(2). Approve the pro-forma first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office adoption, and officer appointments. Authorize banking resolutions, payment processor agreements for cash-on-delivery settlement, and the AML compliance policy.
required_dossiers: First board resolution (written consent or meeting minutes)
Share subscription ledger and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a quorum is not met or an officer declines appointment, reconvene by unanimous written consent resolution and fill vacancies by subsequent board resolution; defects are cured retroactively by ratification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); Alberta Treasury Board and Finance (Tax and Revenue Administration); WCB-Alberta.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for a Business Number (BN) via CRA Form RC1 or the Business Registration Online portal. Open a GST/HST account (mandatory once worldwide taxable supplies exceed C$30,000; voluntary registration permitted). Register payroll account if employees are hired. Alberta corporate income tax is administered through CRA on behalf of Alberta; no provincial sales tax applies. Register with WCB-Alberta for mandatory workers' compensation coverage.
required_dossiers: Bank account information for direct deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN registration is delayed, contact CRA Business Registration (1-800-959-5525) with the Certificate of Incorporation; correct misdescribed activities and request retroactive GST/HST registration effective from incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Premises Zoning Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal licensing and development authority (e.g., City of Calgary Business Licence, City of Edmonton Revenue and Licensing, or county/municipal district office).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm whether the municipality requires a general business licence for mail-order retail with fulfillment storage. File the business licence application with premise use disclosure. Ensure zoning compliance for any warehouse (commercial/industrial classification) or confirm home-based business eligibility if operating from a residence. Obtain the municipal occupancy permit and fire inspection clearance as applicable.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Status
Floor plan and zoning letter from municipal planning
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence is refused due to zoning, apply for a discretionary use approval or minor variance; appeal the decision to the applicable subdivision and development appeal board; or relocate to conforming commercial premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No provincial industrial licensing authority applies to ISIC 4791 mail-order retail; municipal business licensing authority (e.g., City of Calgary or City of Edmonton Revenue and Licensing) may apply depending on premises location.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Business Licence (municipal, where required by local by-law); no federal or provincial operational permit applies to cash-on-delivery e-commerce retailing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — registration and full EIA are not required for mail-order retail and fulfillment warehousing; no Schedule 1 activity under the Environmental Assessment (Mandatory and Exempted Activities) Regulation, AR 13/2012, is engaged.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Non-industrial office and warehouse occupancy: no process wastewater discharge; compliance with municipal sewer use by-laws for sanitary connections; packaging waste directed to municipal recycling and diversion programs; returned and defective goods (electronics, batteries) handled under the Alberta Recycling Management Regulation, AR 60/2004, and EPEA waste management requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code, AR 39/2004, for storage occupancy including emergency exits, extinguishers, and alarm systems; municipal occupancy permit and structural inspection for any fulfillment premises; workplace hazard assessment under the Occupational Health and Safety Code, AR 87/2009, covering manual handling, ergonomics, and contractor safety for delivery operations; mandatory WCB-Alberta employer coverage for workers; electrical installation permits under the Safety Codes Act, SA 2004, c S-0.5, as adopted through the Alberta Electrical Safety Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident corporation must apply to the CRA for a Business Number (BN) before registering for GST/HST or opening a payroll account. If the corporation carries on business in Canada or makes taxable supplies in Canada, it must register through the CRA's 'Register a GST/HST account' service, Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and GST/HST Account), or the online Business Registration Online (BRO) portal. The corporation must provide its legal name, operating name, business address, date of incorporation, and Canadian agent/representative details if applicable. After identity verification, the CRA issues a 9-digit BN followed by a 2-character program account code (e.g., RT for GST/HST). Foreign corporations without a physical Canadian establishment may designate a representative or use a registered agent to facilitate registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide US-style check-the-box elections. Corporations incorporated in Canada are treated as separate taxable entities under the Income Tax Act. Available elections relevant to this structure include: (i) a corporation may elect to be a 'Canadian-controlled private corporation' (CCPC) if it meets the statutory residency, ownership, and capital tests; (ii) associated corporations may file an agreement to allocate the federal small business deduction limit under section 125 of the Income Tax Act; (iii) GST/HST registrants may elect the Quick Method of accounting under CRA administrative policy; and (iv) non-resident corporations earning Canadian-source rental income may file an election under subsection 216(1) of the Income Tax Act to compute tax on a net basis. There is no tax transparency election for a solvent Canadian corporation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) in participating provinces; Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies made in Canada per single calendar quarter or over the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (small supplier threshold under the Excise Tax Act). Non-resident e-commerce operators supplying goods to Canadian customers through a Canadian distribution/fulfilment centre are generally deemed to be making taxable supplies in Canada and may be required to register regardless of traditional physical-presence rules, subject to de minimis rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada currently has no mandatory national electronic invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance regime. The CRA accepts electronic invoices (EDI, PDF, XML) if they contain the prescribed GST/HST information set out in the Excise Tax Act and the New Harmonized Value-added Tax Regulations. Participation in the Pan-Canadian e-invoicing standard (PEPPOL) is voluntary. There is no API-based tax clearance, digital stamping, or pre-clearance authorization requirement for commercial invoices before export.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under section 3 of Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act applies to supplies of goods exported by the vendor, provided the goods are delivered outside Canada and the vendor has evidence of export. For e-commerce mail-order retail with cash-on-delivery, the seller must establish that (a) title to the goods passes outside Canada or the goods are physically exported as documented, (b) the buyer is a non-resident and is not in Canada at the time of delivery, and (c) the export occurs within a reasonable time. Offshore services supplied to non-residents may also be zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI, subject to exclusions for services delivered to a person in Canada or where the primary benefit is received in Canada. Cash-on-delivery remittances routed through local logistics partners must be clearly tied to the export transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency Form B13A or electronic equivalent transmitted via CES/CDS system)
Bill of Lading or air waybill evidencing shipment to a foreign destination

Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank/payment processor evidence (CAD remittance from foreign buyer or its designated logistics/courier agent) supporting actual cash-on-delivery collection outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may re-assess GST/HST, deny zero-rating, and recover the notional 5% GST on the full selling price if contemporaneous export documentation is absent or if goods are later returned to Canada or sold to a domestic buyer. Penalties under the Excise Tax Act include a failure-to-file penalty of 1% of net tax for each complete month up to 12 months (minimum CAD 100) for missing returns; a false-statement penalty of the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the understated tax where knowingly or under circumstances amounting to gross negligence; and interest accruing on unpaid tax at the prescribed rate. Criminal fraud penalties apply where false certificates or export documents are knowingly furnished. For income tax, the CRA may impose a 50% gross-negligence penalty under subsection 163(2) of the Income Tax Act and prosecute fraudulent invoicing schemes. Where an exporter claims zero-rating on Cash-on-Delivery transactions, the CRA will scrutinize the seller's internal controls, logistics partner agreements, and FX remittance trail to ensure the goods were actually exported and that payment was collected outside Canada within the stipulated 180-day period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a floating exchange rate regime with unrestricted convertibility for current account transactions under the Payments, Clearing and Settlement Act. Capital account transactions are liberalized, enabling free repatriation of corporate profits, dividends, and capital gains for resident corporations subject only to standard tax compliance and beneficial ownership disclosure. Profit remittance hurdles remain minimal for established Alberta-incorporated entities, requiring no prior approval for routine distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export receipts applies in Canada. Exporters may retain foreign currency proceeds in offshore or domestic accounts without prescribed timelines. Banks may request documentation for financing or AML verification, but no regulatory conversion ratios or deadlines exist for mail-order retail settlements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility rating for platforms such as Airwallex in facilitating cross-border e-commerce remittances. Legal constraints include mandatory FINTRAC registration as a money services business and full adherence to the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act for any offshore digital EMI operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote corporate account opening is permitted via video KYC and electronic signatures for most tier-one banks; however, directors and authorized signers must complete in-person or live video interviews for enhanced due diligence in medium-risk cash-on-delivery e-commerce sectors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained high-volume inbound COD remittances exceeding normal business patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate charter, articles of incorporation, director and shareholder registers, recent bank statements, export contracts, tax filings, and source-of-funds affidavits

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or shell company indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ultimate beneficial owner declarations, corporate structure charts, and independent verification reports

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound wires processed via SWIFT MT103 using purpose codes such as CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION or EQUITY INVESTMENT. All transactions require matching corporate account details, beneficial ownership certification, and source-of-funds documentation. FINTRAC reporting thresholds apply to suspicious or large-value movements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements cleared primarily through SWIFT MT103 for trade payables. Commercial Letters of Credit are available via correspondent banking relationships. For cash-on-delivery retail model, disbursements align with logistics partner remittances and must reference commercial invoices and delivery proofs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Registrar of Corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or amalgamation; recurring anniversary-based deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 60 per delinquent year; failure to file for two consecutive years authorizes the Registrar to issue a 120-day dissolution notice and administratively strike the corporation off the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including Alberta corporate income tax allocation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Calgary Tax Services Office, administering Alberta corporate income tax under the federal-provincial tax collection agreement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (December 31 year-end due June 30); tax year determined by corporate election.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: ITA s. 162(1) failure-to-file penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; repeat non-filers face 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months; daily arrears interest under ITA s. 161(1).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Return (annual or periodic filing dependent on revenue and reporting-period election)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) GST/HST Electronic Filing Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers: due within 3 months after fiscal year-end; quarterly and monthly filers: due within 1 month after each reporting period; e-commerce COD retailer must register once the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold is exceeded.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Excise Tax Act s. 280 failure-to-file and failure-to-register penalties of 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per complete month, maximum 12 months, with arrears interest; gross-negligence penalty of 5% of the unreported amount may also apply.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: ABCA imposes no size-based compulsory audit for private corporations. The corporation must prepare and present annual financial statements to members, but members may waive the appointment of an auditor by unanimous resolution each year; mandatory audit is triggered only by shareholder requisition, court order, or applicable regulated-sector legislation (bank, trust, insurance, or public issuer).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: CPA Canada Handbook: IFRS (Part I) is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises and optional for private corporations; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, Part II) is the customary framework for a private Alberta e-commerce corporation; tax-basis reporting is not a stand-alone GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta Corporate Transparency Act and ABCA require a private corporation to maintain a current Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register recording any person with direct or indirect 25%-or-greater ownership or control; the register must be updated within 15 days of a share-transfer-driven change and confirmed annually against the share register; no separate ISC filing is delivered to the Alberta Corporate Registry, but the register must be produced to tax and law-enforcement authorities on demand.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)
Securities Register and Records of Share Transfers
Accounting Records (books, contracts, invoices, and underlying vouchers)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–1,100 per year (CAD 400–1,500) for registered office and corporate agent services in Alberta
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–10,000 per year (CAD 4,000–13,500) if an auditor is appointed; commonly avoided by unanimous member waiver under ABCA

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal and Alberta general corporate income tax rate: 23% (15% federal Part I rate plus 8% Alberta general rate, effective January 1, 2020).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs) pay an effective combined rate of 11% on the first CA$500,000 of active business income (9% federal Small Business Deduction rate plus 2% Alberta small business rate). Other incentives: 13% federal Manufacturing and Processing profits rate; refundable Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits; 100% immediate expensing of eligible manufacturing and processing machinery; non-capital losses are deductible against income for 20 years with a 3-year carry-back.
